# theme

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/theme"
```

Package theme is the palette and the lipgloss styles every bezel app draws with.

<a name="All"></a>
## func [All](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L193>)

```go
func All() map[string]Theme
```

All returns all built\-in theme presets keyed by their CLI name. Useful for \-\-theme flag validation and \-\-list\-themes output in host CLIs.

<a name="DarkTerminal"></a>
## func [DarkTerminal](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L281>)

```go
func DarkTerminal() bool
```

DarkTerminal asks the terminal on stdin/stdout whether its background is dark, for code that resolves a theme outside a running bubbletea program. A redirected stdin or stdout is not asked, and reads as dark.

<a name="Category"></a>
## type [Category](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L216-L219>)

Category groups a set of related built\-in theme names for display purposes \- e.g. a \-\-list\-themes command that wants headings instead of one flat list.

```go
type Category struct {
    Name   string
    Themes []string // names, in display order; each is also a key in All()
}
```

<a name="Categories"></a>
### func [Categories](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L223>)

```go
func Categories() []Category
```

Categories returns the built\-in themes grouped for display. Every theme in All\(\) belongs to exactly one category.

<a name="Colors"></a>
## type [Colors](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L17-L35>)

Colors names what a colour is for, not where one app happens to use it. Each value is a lipgloss colour string: a hex value \("\#7C3AED"\) or an ANSI code \("63"\). Empty means the adaptive default for that role.

```go
type Colors struct {
    // Background is the whole screen, behind every pane; it decides light or
    // dark itself. Empty leaves the terminal's own.
    Background string
    Accent     string // focused borders, section headings, legend keys
    Selection  string // the cursor row, the focused panel's title
    Border     string // unfocused borders, status and hint text
    Dim        string // secondary text, items not yet present
    Text       string // body text
    Success    string // present items, healthy results
    Warning    string // drafts, soft failures
    Danger     string // errors, unknown items
    Info       string // counts, badges, neutral highlights
    OnAccent   string // text drawn on a filled accent, success, warning or danger
    // Series tells apart things of one kind, such as a dashboard's panels;
    // Ramp climbs from low to high, as a meter or a graph fills.
    Series [6]string
    Ramp   [3]string
}
```

<a name="Resolved"></a>
## type [Resolved](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/resolved.go#L16-L59>)

Resolved is a Theme after the whole cascade has been applied: ready\-to\-use lipgloss styles plus the colors they were derived from. A consumer builds one per instance and only reads it afterwards.

```go
type Resolved struct {
    Colors Colors

    // Background and Foreground are for tea.View's fields of the same names:
    // the theme's Background and Text, or nil to keep the terminal's.
    Background color.Color
    Foreground color.Color

    // Text styles for content that says what kind of thing it is.
    Success      lipgloss.Style
    Warning      lipgloss.Style
    Danger       lipgloss.Style
    Info         lipgloss.Style
    Accent       lipgloss.Style
    Dim          lipgloss.Style // secondary text
    Muted        lipgloss.Style // hints and gutters, quieter than Dim
    Key          lipgloss.Style // a key name in running text
    Bold         lipgloss.Style
    Section      lipgloss.Style // a heading inside a list
    TableHeader  lipgloss.Style
    Cursor       lipgloss.Style // the row under the cursor
    Caret        lipgloss.Style // the cell under a text field's caret
    Badge        lipgloss.Style // a filled label; recolour its background per kind
    Match        lipgloss.Style // every search match in a text
    MatchCurrent lipgloss.Style // the match the reader is on
    Selected     lipgloss.Style // text selected in a field

    // Chrome styles the shell draws with. Derived from Colors like the rest.
    Panel        draw.PanelStyle
    PanelFocused draw.PanelStyle
    Chrome       draw.ChromeStyle
    Legend       legend.Style
    StatusOK     lipgloss.Style
    StatusErr    lipgloss.Style
    Modal        lipgloss.Style
    Button       draw.ButtonStyle

    // CaretBlink is how often every text input built with this theme flips its
    // caret; zero is 530ms. Tests shrink it, as each key arms one.
    CaretBlink time.Duration
    // Series and Ramp are Colors' own, as foreground styles.
    Series [6]lipgloss.Style
    Ramp   [3]lipgloss.Style
}
```

<a name="Resolve"></a>
### func [Resolve](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/resolved.go#L63>)

```go
func Resolve(t Theme, dark bool) Resolved
```

Resolve turns t into styles for a dark or light terminal. Steps: the colour cascade, then the styles derived from it.

<a name="Theme"></a>
## type [Theme](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L40-L43>)

Theme layers an appearance: Base is an optional preset \(nil → adaptive default\) that may have a Base of its own; Colors override every layer under them.

```go
type Theme struct {
    Base   *Theme
    Colors Colors
}
```

<a name="Default"></a>
### func [Default](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L233>)

```go
func Default() Theme
```

Default leaves every colour to the adaptive default, light or dark as the terminal is. Each preset builds a fresh Theme: a change never reaches the next.

<a name="Lookup"></a>
### func [Lookup](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/theme/palette.go#L203>)

```go
func Lookup(name string) (Theme, error)
```

Lookup is the built\-in theme called name, in any case; empty is Default. The error names what was asked for; the caller adds where its list is.
